notes: EDITION: this is the 2025 Pittsburgh Steelers Media Guide (IA item steelers-2025-media-guide-pittsburgh-c, dated 2025-07-30; the 2026 guide is not online yet), so through_season is 2024, not 2025. Evidence: the table of contents carries '2024 SEASON IN REVIEW' (final 2024 statistics, game summaries) and no 2025-season section; the record lists end with 2024 entries (Najee Harris 2021-24, Russell Wilson 12/01/2024 at Cincinnati with 414 passing yards, the 'Many; last time by Beanie Bishop Jr. (10/20/2024 vs. N.Y. Jets)' interception line) and none from 2025.

SOURCE: RECORD BOOK, 'STEELERS RECORDS' section, 'All-Time Individual Leaders' (table of contents: printed p. 664). The printed page number is the pdf page minus 1 (pdf p674 prints '2025 MEDIA GUIDE | 673'); every pdf_page here is the pdf page. Lists used: rushing yards p667, rushing touchdowns p668, passing yards p668, touchdown passes p670 (the 'Most Touchdown Passes' heading is at the foot of p669), receptions p670 (game list runs onto p671), receiving yards p671, receiving touchdowns p671, interceptions p673 (game list runs onto p674), sacks p674. Each is a 'Most ...' block with Career, Season and Game sub-lists, ranked by exactly that stat, so all 27 present pairs are kind=list.

REGULAR SEASON: the headings ('Most Yards Rushing', 'Most Quarterback Sacks' ...) do not say regular season or postseason, and no row carries a playoff marker (the guide marks playoff plays with an asterisk and a '* Playoff Game' legend in its Steelers/Opponent Longest Plays lists, pdf pp. 542-543, but not here). The guide's separate postseason pages (table of contents: 538 Steelers Postseason Experience, 539 Steelers in the Postseason, 556 The Last Time (Postseason), 559 Division Playoff Races) are results, experience and last-time lists, not leader lists, and none of them were used; so these lists are taken as the regular-season record book, but the guide itself does not say so.

RANKS AND TIES: the guide prints the rank number only on the first row of a tie group; the tied rows below it have a blank rank cell. Ranks here follow the printed numbers (competition ranking, e.g. 1, 2, 2, 2, 5) and every row of a tie group carries the shared rank with tie=true. Rows that were typed under such a blank rank cell have raw text without a rank number.

TRUNCATION: career and season lists are top-10 blocks and are complete (ties can make them run a row or two past 10). Game lists vary; where a tie group at the end is long it was not copied and scope_note says what is printed (passing yards game: 23 rows printed, first 10 copied; touchdown passes game: 35 rows printed, first 8 copied, the 27-game 4-TD group left out; receptions game: 54 rows printed, first 16 copied; receiving yards game: 21 rows printed, first 10 copied). complete_to is the number of rows the guide prints, rows[] is what was copied.

FORMAT: 'raw' is the printed row as read: name, then the career span or the game date and opponent in parentheses, then an optional position tag such as (TE) or (RB) printed after the parentheses, then the value. Career spans are as printed ('1995-02' two-digit end years, '1982-87,89-91' without a space, 'Diontae Johnson (2019-)' in the receptions list but '(2019-23)' in the receiving-yards list; both kept exactly). Game 'years' is the printed date MM/DD/YYYY exactly as printed; the opponent stays in raw. Active players (for example T.J. Watt, Cameron Heyward) are printed in bold.

SACKS: the heading is 'Most Quarterback Sacks' with no 'since 1982' qualifier and the lists include careers that began before sacks were official (L.C. Greenwood 1969-81, Joe Greene 1969-81, Joe Greene's 5.0 on 12/10/1972, L.C. Greenwood's 4.5 on 11/25/1979), so pre-1982 sack numbers are the club's unofficial counts.

TWO ODDITIES KEPT AS PRINTED (uncertain=true on both rows): (1) the season sacks list prints 'T.J. Watt (2023)' twice, once with 19.0 at rank 2 and once with 14.0 in the rank-8 tie group; checked at 400 dpi, both really print (2023), so the season label of the 14.0 row may be a misprint in the guide. (2) the rushing game list prints 'Najee Harris (01/03/2021 vs. Cleveland) 188' (checked at 400 dpi), but the same guide prints his career span as 2021-24 and his reception game as 09/26/2021, so a January 2021 date does not fit; the value and name are clear. Nothing was changed. All other game rows were checked against the players' printed career spans (a January game counts for the previous season) and fit.

CHECKS: every row was typed from 200-260 dpi crops of the page pictures (OCR text was only used to find pages); values were checked to fall with rank and each printed rank number was checked against its tie group (rank = 1 + number of larger values), with no mismatches. Tackles: no list in any scope, see 'missing'.
